sections.title: Career & Wealth
sections.lead: You may approach organizing work through questioning assumptions and working through language.
sections.text:
You may bring questioning assumptions and working through language to organizing work. Jù Mén is a major star associated with this style of attention. Here it occupies the [[term:palace.career]] (guān lù gōng) — a chart area describing how you take responsibility, learn professionally and arrange a task. You may question a claim that others accept quickly and want to understand what supports it. At the beginning of a project, notice whether you naturally clarify the aim, research a method, check details or coordinate handovers. A useful question can sound like rejection when the other person is not ready for an extended examination. The reading explores a working style without assigning you a profession; skills, interests and the conditions of a role matter together. Try establishing a shared aim before raising the question most likely to clarify it. A useful next step is to choose one part of an existing workflow and agree with a colleague on an observable improvement. Let the response you receive guide a small adjustment; the placement offers a question to explore in your own circumstances.
At the same time,
You may bring personal boundaries and value based choices to working with your network. Lián Zhēn  is a major star associated with this style of attention. Here it occupies the [[term:palace.friends]] (jiāo yǒu gōng) — a chart area describing exchanges among friends, team members and people you collaborate with. You may invest strongly in choices that express your values and notice when a boundary feels blurred. If a group plans an event, distinguish those offering ideas, those owning tasks and those available only for occasional support. A disagreement about a process can become personal when feelings and principles are treated as one thing. Friendship can coexist with a work agreement, but familiarity should not substitute for a clear handover or scope of authority. Try separating observable facts, your feelings and the specific change you are requesting. A useful next step is to write down the owner and completion point for one shared task. Let the response you receive guide a small adjustment; the placement offers a question to explore in your own circumstances.
You may bring coordination, fairness and procedural care to working with your network. Tiān Xiàng  is a major star associated with this style of attention. Here it occupies the Friends Palace (jiāo yǒu gōng) — a chart area describing exchanges among friends, team members and people you collaborate with.…
